title: Microburst throughput calibration + p95 drift detector for model-suite
creator: Marco Liu
description: Purpose: Build and maintain a tokens/sec microbenchmark harness focused on detecting small but meaningful regressions in p95 and short-duration throughput (microbursts) across core model variants. This ticket covers the harness design, synthetic workload generation (microburst and steady-state), stable seeding for repeatability, CI integration with regression gates, and a simple alerting rule that flags directional drift in p95 or ~10% regression in sustained tokens/sec. Rationale: Existing throughput suites catch long-running regressions but miss short-duration behavior changes (microbursts) and small p95 shifts that still impact interactive UX. The new harness should be cheap to run in CI, deterministic enough for daily runs, and instrumented to feed our observability dashboards and the regression detector service.
acceptance_criteria: Harness can run headless in CI and complete within 25 minutes for the core-model matrix (4 model flavors x 3 prompt families)
Collects tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99, and CPU/GPU utilization per worker with consistent naming and tags
Synthetic workload includes: short bursts (100-800 tokens), conversational chains (20-200 tokens), and long-context streams (>2048) where supported
Regression detector alerts when p95 increases by >8% relative to rolling baseline OR sustained tokens/sec drops >10% over 3 consecutive CI runs
Results automatically upload to the throughput dashboard with a permalink and a CI artifact; failing runs attach a perf-diff summary to the PR
Bench harness respects model-variant pinning and KV cache warm-start behavior (can run cold and warm modes)
Playbooks and runbook documented in the ticket and linked from the console metrics panel
tasks: Design: define microburst workload flavours, seed strategy, and measurement windows
Engineering: implement runner that supports multithreaded clients, warm/cold cache modes, and configurable concurrency
Dataset: create deterministic prompt families: short-qna, convo-chain, long-seq; include optional randomness seeds
Metrics: standardize metric names (throughput.tokens_per_sec, latency.p95_ms, worker.gpu_util_pct)
Dashboard: add per-model flicker chart, historical baseline bands, and failed-run diff view
Regression detector: wire CI artifacts into regression service, implement rule thresholds and notification channels
CI: add scheduled daily job and PR gate that runs lightweight smoke variant
Canary: run a 1hr canary on dedicated pool after major runtime changes and link results
regressions_policy: Primary detection: compare current run to rolling baseline (last 14 daily runs) using percent-change and a bootstrap confidence interval. Flag if p95 increases >8% with p-value <0.05 OR sustained tokens/sec drop >10% across 3 consecutive runs. Secondary checks: high variance (>20% stdev across identical workers) triggers flaky-run classification and requires manual triage. On alert, post to #perf-alerts with link to artifact, CI job, and suggested triage steps.
rollout_plan: Week 1: finalize workload specs, implement runner API and deterministic seeding
Week 2: instrument metrics and add dashboard ingestion; create synthetic prompt families
Week 3: CI integration with scheduled nightly jobs and lightweight PR smoke tests
Week 4: enable regression detector rules and route alerts to oncall; run canary against dedicated pool
Post-launch: monitor false positive rate for 2 weeks and adjust thresholds or smoothing parameters

notes: Trade-offs: Shorter runs reduce cost but increase variance. We choose daily scheduled full-run + lightweight PR smoke to balance costs and signal quality.
Statistical approach: prefer bootstrap + percent-change instead of raw z-score due to non-normal latency tails.
If we see repeat false positives, switch to a two-tier rule: require both percent-change and exceeding historical volatility band.
Security: bench harness will not send payloads to external telemetry; artifacts are sanitized and stored in internal CI bucket.
